faqs.answer: GAIA works in WhatsApp and Telegram as well as on the web. You text it tasks the same way, and it sees your email and calendar when it acts.
faqs.question: Can I text GAIA like Instinct?

faqs.answer: GAIA offers a free tier, and Pro is a flat ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month. There is no per-task metering and no hardware to buy.

faqs.answer: Connect Gmail and Google Calendar first so GAIA has context. Then connect Slack, Notion, or your task tool. Most people delegate their first errand within minutes.

gaiaAdvantages: Text GAIA in WhatsApp and Telegram, the same habit you already have
Reads email and calendar before acting, so errands fit your schedule
Graph-based memory that carries context across weeks and months
50+ integrations instead of one texting channel
Open source with a free tier, self-hostable via Docker
gaiaReplaces: Travel and errand requests you currently text to Instinct
Copying booking details into your calendar by hand
Following up on errands across separate apps
Keeping trip context in your head instead of your assistant
metaDescription: Need an Instinct alternative with more reach? GAIA texts back in WhatsApp and Telegram, and adds open-source email and calendar help.
metaTitle: Best Instinct Alternative: Open-Source SMS AI
migrationSteps: List the errands you text to Instinct most: travel, bookings, reminders
Connect Gmail and Google Calendar so GAIA has your schedule and inbox
Message GAIA in WhatsApp or Telegram with your next errand
Review how GAIA connects the errand to your calendar, then keep delegating
name: Instinct
painPoints: Instinct handles one errand at a time over text, with no view into your inbox or calendar
Waitlist-era access means availability and features keep shifting
Travel and errands are covered, but email triage and scheduling live elsewhere
Closed product with no self-hosted option and no public roadmap
Context resets per conversation instead of building across weeks
tagline: Errands by text are nice. Context makes them stick.
whyPeopleLook: Instinct proves that texting an errand beats opening an app. But users outgrow the single channel: the errand still needs calendar checks, inbox context, and follow-through that a text thread cannot see. People looking for an Instinct alternative want the same texting habit backed by an assistant that already knows their schedule and their inbox.
